description:
Found by the fz-kdt.198 refutation (2026-09-03). PRE-EXISTING at accb5cfbe
and unchanged by 198. arrow_set_covers (contract.rs) asks
is_subtype(tuple(args), domain) over the ground clause rows, and the
callable positions pass whatever arrow arrives: a `(binary) -> int` at a
declared `(utf8) -> int` is accepted (correct: parameters are contravariant,
binary is wider), but so is the reverse, and so is `(integer) -> int` at
`(binary) -> int`, which no value can satisfy. Either arrow subtyping is not
contravariant in the parameter at this seam or the coverage check erases the
callable position before comparing -- the ticket's first step is to say
which, with the calculator answer for is_subtype((integer)->int,
(binary)->int) quoted. Reproducers (198 research archive):

s9:
import Utf8

defmodule M do
  @spec apply1(((binary) -> integer)) :: integer
  fn apply1(_f), do: 1
end

@spec narrow(utf8) :: integer
fn narrow(_b), do: 2

fn main() do
  dbg(M.apply1(&narrow/1))
end

s10:
defmodule M do
  @spec apply1(((binary) -> integer)) :: integer
  fn apply1(_f), do: 1
end

@spec narrow(integer) :: integer
fn narrow(_b), do: 2

fn main() do
  dbg(M.apply1(&narrow/1))
end

Sibling of fz-kdt.201 (the @spec RETURN side is unchecked): together they
are the two halves of "a @spec is not a contract on callables". Concordant:
fz-kdt.184 (instantiation polarity for @spec variables under arrow
parameters -- that ticket makes the VARIABLE side contravariant; this one is
the GROUND arrow) and fz-kdt.132 (closure clause arrows are evidence, not a
contract -- the callee side of the same seam). Red-first: s9 and s10 report
spec/violation on three doors while the correct-direction case
(`(binary) -> int` at `(utf8) -> int`) keeps printing.
title: [BUG] A callable argument's DOMAIN is not checked at a @spec argument position: `(integer) -> int` is accepted where `(binary) -> int` is declared, and the reverse
